## Summary

The MCP client URL every doc and committed example specifies —
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/` (WITH the trailing slash) — answers `307` with
`location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, an HTTPS->HTTP scheme downgrade. No HSTS
header is present to upgrade it back. Re-reproduced 2026-08-27 with unauthenticated probes; the
no-slash form `/mcp` returns a correct `401` with a Bearer challenge.

A 307 preserves method and body, and clients differ on whether they retain `Authorization`
across a same-host scheme change. A client that retains it transmits its bearer PAT in
plaintext; one that drops it still sends the body in the clear. The documentation points AT the
affected form: `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:18`, `docs/mcp-client-setup.md:54,73,96`,
`docs/mcp-auth.md:252`.

## Confirmed root cause

Proven at runtime by a discriminating experiment; the full evidence, the experiment and the
defect attribution are in the RCA comment on this ticket. Three changeable artifacts:

**A** `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127` is a PREFIX `location /mcp` with a URI-preserving
`proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;`, so the external `/mcp/` reaches the app verbatim while the app
mounts at `http_path = "/mcp"` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:524,618-627`); Starlette's default
`redirect_slashes` emits the 307. `docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271` already prescribes EXACT-MATCH
locations for this asymmetry and the template diverged from it.

**B** uvicorn is built at `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:311-317` with no `forwarded_allow_ips`, so
it defaults from the environment (`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`, default `"127.0.0.1"`). The app
runs in a container (`docker-compose.yml:337` binds `0.0.0.0`, published `127.0.0.1:8091:8091`),
so nginx's connection arrives from the docker bridge gateway; the peer is untrusted, nginx's
`X-Forwarded-Proto https` (`rebar.conf.template:132`) is dropped, and app-generated absolute
URLs are built as `http://`. No `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set in `infra/`.

**C** The 443 server block has no `add_header Strict-Transport-Security`; a repo-wide grep for
`strict-transport` returns zero hits.

## Approach

1. **Serve `/mcp/` directly instead of redirecting.** Adopt the documented exact-match pattern
   (`docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271`), specialized to the named upstream: `location = /mcp/` and
   `location = /mcp`, both `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp/mcp;`, each carrying the existing SSE
   settings (`proxy_http_version 1.1`, cleared `Connection`, `proxy_buffering off`,
   `proxy_read_timeout 3600s`). An exact-match location with a URI on `proxy_pass` replaces the
   matched URI, so `/mcp/` arrives at the app as `/mcp` and `redirect_slashes` never fires — no
   Location header is produced at all. The PREFIX `location /mcp` is retained for `/mcp/...`
   sub-paths, so nothing that works today stops.
2. **Make a plaintext Location structurally impossible.** Add `proxy_redirect http://$host/
   https://$host/;` and the named-upstream form to the MCP locations, so nginx upgrades any
   `http://` Location an upstream might emit. Scoped to the MCP locations deliberately:
   `proxy_redirect` defaults to `default`, which derives its rewrite from that location's own
   `proxy_pass`, so declaring explicit rules at SERVER level would replace that default for
   `/review/` and `/opcert/` and could break their relative redirects.
3. **Fix the scheme derivation.** Set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` on the `mcp` compose service so
   uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` trusts nginx's forwarded proto. No code change is needed
   (uvicorn reads the variable natively), and it corrects every app-generated absolute URL, not
   only this Location. Spoofing is not a new risk: nginx sets `proxy_set_header
   X-Forwarded-Proto https;` as a LITERAL, so a client-supplied value is always overwritten
   before the app sees it, and the container port is published on host loopback with nginx as
   the sole reachable client — the posture `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE=true` acknowledges.
4. **Add HSTS.** `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
   always;` on the 443 server block. `always` is required so it is emitted on error responses —
   the 401 the MCP endpoint returns to an unauthenticated client.

NOT changed: `EXPECTED_URL` in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py` and the
documented/example client URLs. After step 1 the trailing-slash form is served directly over
https with no redirect, so it is safe and stays canonical, and keeping it holds
`auth_resource_server_url` (the OAuth audience) consistent with the committed examples.

NOT changed: production nginx on the live box. This proposes the config in the repo; applying it
is an operator step (`nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The edge routes `/mcp/` straight to the app's `/mcp`, so no Location header is produced
      for the documented URL. Verified by a structural parse of
      `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` asserting an exact-match `location = /mcp/` whose
      `proxy_pass` carries the app path `/mcp`.
- [ ] An HSTS header with `max-age` of at least 31536000 is served on the 443 server, marked
      `always` so it is present on the unauthenticated 401. Verified by a structural parse
      asserting `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "..." always;` inside that server block.
- [ ] Each MCP location carries a `proxy_redirect` mapping an `http://` upstream Location to
      `https://`. Verified by a structural parse that fails when the directive is absent from
      any MCP location.
- [ ] With the committed `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` value in force, a `/mcp/` request through the
      real `streamable_http_app()` yields a Location whose scheme is `https`. Verified by an
      in-process ASGI test through uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware`, with an untrusted-peer
      negative control asserting `http` so the assertion cannot pass vacuously; plus a
      structural assertion that `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set on the compose `mcp` service.

## Testing

RED-first; both tiers observed failing before any fix.

- `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` — structural tests over the committed nginx template
  (exact-match `/mcp/` and `/mcp` locations, `proxy_redirect` on each MCP location, HSTS with
  `always`) and over `docker-compose.yml` (`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` on the `mcp` service). No nginx
  binary is available here, so these parse the committed text — the approach the existing
  `test_nginx_mcp_location_proxies_to_the_named_upstream` (`:154`) already uses.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — a behavioural test over the real
  `streamable_http_app()` through `uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers.ProxyHeadersMiddleware`
  configured from the committed compose value, asserting the Location scheme is `https`, with an
  untrusted-peer negative control asserting `http`. Executable oracle for mechanism B.

Mutation check: re-introduce each confirmed cause (drop the exact-match locations; drop
`proxy_redirect`; drop the HSTS header; drop `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`) and confirm the
corresponding test returns to RED, then restore. Run inside an OS sandbox.

## File impact

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`,
`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py`.

## Compat / rollback

Additive: two exact-match locations ahead of the retained prefix location, two directives per
MCP location, one HSTS header, one compose env var. `/mcp` returns a 401 today and continues to;
`/mcp/` stops redirecting and starts serving. No caller depends on the 307 — it is the defect.
Rollback is a revert of the four files. Trust boundary unchanged: the `static` bearer still
gates `/mcp`, `/health` stays unauthenticated, and `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` only selects which
peer's `X-Forwarded-*` uvicorn trusts.

## Portability

Committed config plus tests that parse committed text. No CI provider is involved: the
structural tests run under plain `pytest` anywhere, and the behavioural test is in-process ASGI
with no docker and no network. Applying the nginx change is an operator step, not a CI trigger.
